findings.premise: Existing content hashing and BUILD writer ownership provide reusable foundations, but persistent display-bound presentation tokens require new functionality.

findings.premise: Relaying insrc_present tokens into the VS Code panel completes the session-bound MCP-to-panel approval path.
findings.evidence: MCP unaryRpc and the extension's shared rpc are separate transports. The presenter currently opens documents only for a tool-call with ev.present; the panel then performs its own client.content read. The proposed sequence requires a display acknowledgement before insrc_present, but defines neither a pre-present opening/read relay nor how the MCP readId/session becomes the panel's acknowledged read/session. The token sink carries artifactId/token only. A panel read under session B cannot acknowledge the MCP read under session A, and forwarding A's token through B conflicts with the proposed session-bound approval gate. findings.premise: The specified Kotlin transport support and TUI change sites fully migrate both clients to read→display-ack→present→approve.
findings.evidence: JetBrains ArtifactReviewViewDto has no contentVersion/readId. ArtifactContentPane.render calls b.loadHTML(html) or assigns nativeArea.text, while doApprove calls gateway.approve(repo, md, overrideReason). Those rendering and decision owners are absent from the change inventory; adding a session to UnixSocketDaemonRpc cannot create a display acknowledgement or carry a token through these signatures. The TUI's 'a' action directly calls the synchronous svc.workflow.approve(item.path), whose service invokes approveArtifactByJsonPath; no artifact-content display flow exists there. The LLD names TUI files and cross-host tests but supplies no replacement rendering/acknowledgement and approval contracts. findings.premise: The proposed insrc_read response supplies reviewable, versionable content for document-less AMD records through deliveryEvidence.
findings.evidence: The delivery Markdown port excludes AMD from MD_KINDS and returns null for it. handleDeliveryEvidence supplies amendment content through meta/body, with renderedMarkdown=null. The proposed insrc_read signature returns only artifactId, kind, optional renderedMarkdown, contentVersion and readId; it omits meta/body and defines no AMD renderer or canonical version input. The existing VS Code adapter substitutes '# <id>\n\n(no rendered document)' when Markdown is null. findings.premise: The proposed acknowledgement checks make a presentation token proof that content actually reached a display.
findings.evidence: §2.2 returns session-correlated readId/contentVersion to the MCP caller, and §2.3 exposes insrc_display_ack to that same caller. summary.prose: Present-before-approve bound to a provably displayed version under a server-owned, resumable session: the daemon issues a sessionId at session open (validated per request, propagated to workers, never the client envelope); the cross-host path is complete — insrc_read → render → insrc_display_ack → insrc_present({ documents, versions }) → tokens in the tool result → insrc_workflow_approve({ ..., presentToken }), with the VS Code presenter relaying tokens into the panel and decideNow forwarding them. Approvals validate token+version under per-artifact locks and consume tokens; BUILD approval additionally requires its sibling CR fully published (staged-marker + JSON/md agreement, CR-lock-before-BUILD ordering). Review publication is crash-safe; rejected non-AMD reopens token-validated; AMD stays terminal; every writer is inside the locked inventory; steering/guides update as one coordinated change with fail-closed legacy hosts.
